<style>

Each example below is the Backing Track band in one style. Press ▶ Play, then flip **Site** and **MODX** while it plays
(or press **m**), or tick **Switch every … bars** to hear them take turns. Mark which sounds better under each one; the
tally is at the top. The MODX plays each instrument on its Part of the Site Band Performance and the drums on the kit for
that style (set on [Play the Band on the MODX](modx-band.qmd)); an instrument with no Part stays on the site.

## Connect and switch

```{=html}
<div class="ab-bar">
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-primary" id="ab-connect">Connect the MODX</button>
  <span id="ab-status" class="ab-note">Not connected</span>
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" id="ab-site">Site</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" id="ab-modx">MODX</button>
  <label><input type="checkbox" id="ab-auto"> Switch every <input type="number" id="ab-bars" min="1" max="16" value="2"> bars</label>
  <span id="ab-now" class="ab-now"></span>
</div>
<p class="ab-note">The automatic switch times bars from the tempo, not from the band itself, so it can land a little off the barline.
Set the MODX's timing offset on the MODX page first, or the two will not line up.</p>
<p><b>So far:</b> <span id="ab-summary"></span></p>
```
